# 1B.1 Research Note: Vladimir Putin, Russia, 2023

**Bottom line:** the 2023 record is **mostly negative** for 1B.1. I found one formal, pro-restraint policy statement and one limited non-use statement, but they are outweighed by concrete 2023 nuclear signaling in Belarus and explicit use of nuclear posture as coercive leverage against the West.

## Accepted claims

- **Title:** `Указ Президента Российской Федерации от 31.03.2023 г. № 229`  
  **Publisher:** Kremlin  
  **Date:** 31 Mar 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print](https://www.kremlin.ru/acts/bank/49090/print)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin signed an updated Russian foreign-policy concept that explicitly prioritizes strategic stability, preventing global war, reducing risks of nuclear and other WMD use, strengthening arms control, preventing an arms race, and creating conditions for phased reductions in nuclear potentials. This is the strongest 2023 evidence on the pro-restraint side, but it is declaratory policy rather than a concrete de-escalatory act.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.1`, `7A`

- **Title:** `Russia signs deal to deploy tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, says they stay under its control`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via ThePrint  
  **Date:** 25 May 2023  
  **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/](https://theprint.in/world/russia-signs-deal-to-deploy-tactical-nuclear-weapons-in-belarus-says-they-stay-under-its-control/1593879/)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Russia and Belarus formalized the deployment of Russian tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus, described by Moscow as a military-nuclear countermeasure to Western escalation. This is strong evidence **against** 1B.1 because it expands coercive nuclear leverage rather than reducing existential risk.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.1`, `7A`

- **Title:** `Putin says Russia positions nuclear bombs in Belarus as warning to West`  
  **Publisher:** Reuters via Investing.com  
  **Date:** 16 Jun 2023  
  **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/putin-says-russia-positions-nuclear-bombs-in-belarus-as-warning-to-west-3107500)  
  **Claim-level summary:** Putin said the first tactical nuclear warheads had been delivered to Belarus as a warning that the West could not inflict a strategic defeat on Russia. He also said Russia had no need to use nuclear weapons “for now,” but in the same episode he treated arms-reduction talks as a non-starter. Overall, this is escalatory signaling with only limited rhetorical restraint.  
  **Question IDs:** `1B.1`, `7A`

## Search gap

I did **not** find reliable 2023 evidence that Putin took a concrete operational step to reduce nuclear or existential risk, such as withdrawing weapons, cutting alert posture, or re-entering serious arms-control commitments. The best pro-restraint evidence is limited to formal policy language and a conditional “no need for now” statement embedded in an otherwise escalatory Belarus-nuclear episode.

## Working judgment for 1B.1

**Mostly no.** The 2023 pattern looks like **nuclear leverage and coercive escalation**, not a sustained effort to reduce nuclear or existential risk.
